title: Add athena land --pr (owned mode) with a gh REST host client
summary: Retry of the failed PR-landing slice: add an `athena land <job> --pr` command that pushes the job's branch through the push guard, opens the PR, waits for checks, merges, and runs the merged-content check. The host client in a new gh.rs shells out to `gh api` REST endpoints only (no GraphQL). It must contain no email addresses outside athena.toml's email_allow list, which caused the last refusal.

defaults_applied.how: gh.rs and the new command get unit tests with fakes; cargo test and clippy must pass.
No email addresses outside the allow-list, the cause of the earlier refusal, and no tokens in fixtures.
One slice: the command and its host client only.
Use the existing gh CLI rather than an HTTP or octocrab client.
Doc comments and the design and changelog notes are written for outside readers.
The scope was recovered from the quoted prior request, pr.rs, and the design doc.

assumptions: The failed job's only defect was the disallowed email address, so its design is otherwise sound and is redone here.
`gh` is invoked as an external process (gh api), wrapped behind a small command-runner trait so tests need no network or gh binary.
Check waiting polls the REST check-runs and combined status endpoints with a bounded timeout and interval.
Merge uses the REST merge endpoint; the merged commit is found by the stored PR number via the pulls endpoint, never from commit trailers.
The command is `athena land <job> --pr`, in owned mode only; stealth mode stays a later slice.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs implements the pr::Host trait with `gh api` REST calls (pulls create, pulls get, check-runs/status, pulls merge); no `graphql` call or `gh pr` subcommand appears in it.
No file in the change contains an email address outside athena.toml's email_allow list; fixtures use noreply@ or @example.com forms only, or avoid addresses entirely.

A `land` subcommand with a `--pr` flag is added to the CLI. It pushes only via pr::check_push (never forced), stores the PrLink with store_link, waits for checks, merges, then calls check_merged and apply_outcome.
The command exits 0 only when the outcome is Verified/Landed, and 2 for a merged-but-unverified or failed-checks result, matching main.rs's exit-code convention.

Run `cargo test`: new unit tests for gh.rs use a fake command runner, no network. They check the exact REST argument lists, response parsing, and the checks-waiting and merge paths, and all pass together with the existing tests.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean.
docs/design/native-pr-landing.md and CHANGELOG.md note that the command and REST-only host client are done, with the remaining slices (stealth mode and others) still listed as later.

out_of_scope: GraphQL or any gh subcommand other than gh api
Changes to athena.toml, the email allow-list, or other governance files
departures: This is a larger multi-file feature (new host client, a CLI command, tests) than the typical job, so cost and time are higher than the reference. The earlier attempt's admission refusal is a known, avoidable pitfall, which helps the pass rate slightly.
